facts.title: David of Sassoun
facts.text: For more than a thousand years, this epic was carried solely by the voices of storytellers.

facts.title: Four lineages of heroes
facts.text: Sanasar and Balthasar, Mher the Great, David of Sassoun, and Little Mher.

facts.title: A peasant recites it all
facts.text: Bishop Garegin Srvandztiants met Gurbo, who recited the entire tale. Published in Constantinople in 1874.

facts.title: David against the Melik
facts.text: Orphaned and raised in the enemy's land, he returns home and slays the Melik of Msr in single combat.

facts.title: Little Mher waits
facts.text: He enters the cleft of Raven's Rock, where he awaits the end of falsehoods before reappearing.

facts.title: Kochar's statue
facts.text: Yervand Kochar's equestrian statue of David of Sassoun has become the symbol of the capital.

facts.title: December 5, 2012
facts.text: Still told at weddings and celebrations, with the duduk, the epic joins the Intangible Cultural Heritage list.

ytTitle: David of Sassoun, the Armenian epic passed down by word of mouth
ytLead: Passed down orally for more than a thousand years, the epic of David of Sassoun tells of four generations of heroes. Since 2012 it has been on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.
